thread:
mina: Heads-up — ran a microstride pipeline perf pass on staging (microbatch=8, seq=2048). Seeing recurring pipeline stall spikes at the tail that line up with all-reduce waits. attaching traces.

jun: saw the trace. that attention kernel swap to int8 path looks suspicious — kernel select picks it for memory but it serializes some kernels and kills overlap.

dmitri: can you paste the perf snippet? curious about NCCL timings vs kernel exec.

mina: pasted a short extract below:
```
step 1023: forward kernel (attn_int8) 1.9ms
step 1023: allreduce grad_comm 2.7ms (enqueue 0.2ms / wait 2.5ms)
step 1023: backward kernel (ffn_fp16) 2.0ms
pipeline gap: 2.3ms stall
```
runtime-bot: profiler upload complete: https://storage.internal/reports/1829432100/microstride-flame.html

jun: those numbers show comm > single kernel, so overlap is insufficient. runtime is scheduling kernels in-order for memory locality. that helps for RAM but hurts comm/compute overlap here.

sasha: what KV cache behavior did you observe? any cache thrash on prefix tokens?

mina: yes — for shorter prefixes we get a lot of KV-invalidate hits when we switch quantized kernels mid-seq. KV miss causes a small recompute that pushes the timing into the next allreduce epoch.

dmitri: hypothesis: kernel selection policy is too aggressive for int8 on attention for seq>=1024. we should add a heuristic: prefer fp16-attn if predicted comm latency > kernel exec time * 0.6.

jun: or implement a cheap model: if allreduce_estimate > 1.2ms per slice, force fp16-attn for last two layers to preserve overlap.

mina: quick repro command if anyone wants to run locally:
```
./perf_runner --model llama-13b --mp 2 --pp 4 --microbatch 8 --seq 2048 --profiler on --kernel-preference auto
```

sasha: UX note: we should add a flag to pin kernel families per-layer in the deploy config so teams can experiment without rolling new builds.

runtime-bot: rollout note: kernel-policy v2 rolled to canary at 1829400000. if reverting, use `redwoodctl rollout revert kernel-policy v1`.

dmitri: quick experiment — I pinned attn to fp16 for the final 4 layers in the canary. preliminary runs drop stall tail by ~1.8ms and reduce allreduce skew.

jun: good. also try doubling microbatch to 16 for the same throughput target and see if 1F1B (one-forward-one-back) smoothing helps. microbatching increases kernel compute time which can hide allreduce lat.

mina: tried microbatch=16: overall latency up ~6ms per request but tail p99 improved, and token throughput slightly better. needs numbers from cost model.

sasha: on KV side, adding a small per-shard prefix hold cache (keep recent KV across kernel switches) reduced recompute spikes on my run. should be low effort.

dmitri: action items:
- mina: attach full flamegraphs and the microbatch=8 vs 16 CSVs (ETA 2h)
- jun: prototype kernel-policy rule: prefer fp16-attn when comm_est > exec*0.6 (ETA EOD)
- sasha: design config flag for layer-level kernel pinning + prefix-hold KV option (ETA 2 days)

jun: ack. thanks — important win if we can avoid the regressions while keeping int8 for memory-constrained models.
